answer: Sawdust drifts through the sawpit, and the great saw hangs in its frame by the log. Proof of sawyer via plank tally — a plank the sawyer rips only after 23 planks lie flat without one warping at the edge, each ripped by the sawyer himself. summit marks the log and sets the saw to the line. dawn pulls the saw through the timber in long strokes. whisper stacks the planks and checks each one with the straightedge. Twenty-three planks must lie flat without one warping at the edge, and the next still warps where the log ran green.
